newsitem.title: FRANCE: SNCF to start reduced Eurostar service Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: SNCF to start reduced Eurostar service Wednesday.

text.p: France's SNCF national railway said on Tuesday it would begin reduced Eurostar express passenger train service through the Channel Tunnel on Wednesday.

Eurotunnel earlier on Tuesday received the go-ahead from the Inter-Governmental Commission of French and British government authorities to reopen the tunnel to passenger service including the Eurostar.

The tunnel has been closed to all passenger traffic since November 18, when a fire on a truck destroyed a freight shuttle train and severely damaged a 300 metre section of the tunnel, injuring 34 people.
Eurotunnel staged a drill on Sunday to prove that it could safely run passenger services when one of the two rail tunnels is still closed for repairs.

SNCF said it would start reduced service from Wednesday and that it hoped that by Friday, December 6, it would have 13 Paris-London return trips each day and seven Paris-Brussels return trips. This compares with 14 Paris-London trips each weekday and 16 on weekend days under normal circumstances.
"Because of the work Eurotunnel must undertake for several months, the SNCF and its partners regret that only a reduced service can be put in place," SNCF said in a statement.
The Paris-London trip would take between three hours and 20 minutes and three-and-a-half hours because of the damage to the tunnel from the fire. A normal trip takes about three hours, the SNCF said.
SNCF said clients holding a Eurostar reservation should call Eurostar's reservation service to reconfirm tickets as schedules have been changed.
It said that reservation holders unhappy with the new schedule would be eligible for refunds or exchanges free of charge.
